critical_bugs: Unchecked data bounds in all __unpack_* methods will raise struct.error or ValueError when receiving truncated or corrupted UDP packets, causing immediate thread crashes.
No exception handling around binary parsing and network I/O; a single malformed packet will terminate the data/command processing loop without recovery.
warnings: Sockets are instantiated but never explicitly closed in the visible code, leading to file descriptor/resource leaks on restart or abnormal shutdown.
Thread lifecycle management relies on time.sleep for synchronization instead of proper primitives (threading.Event/Lock), risking zombie threads and unsafe shutdown sequences.
Shared mutable state (__is_locked, listeners, sockets) is read/written across threads without mutex protection, creating race conditions during runtime configuration changes.
recommendations: Add strict length validation before slicing data in __unpack_* methods, and wrap parsing logic in try-except blocks to gracefully log and skip corrupted packets.
Implement a dedicated shutdown/cleanup method that explicitly closes sockets (socket.close()) and joins threads using threading.Event for cooperative termination.
Protect shared state modifications with threading.Lock or RLock, particularly around set_* methods and listener assignments, to prevent race conditions.
Externalize hardcoded IP addresses, ports, and multicast settings via configuration files or environment variables to support dynamic deployment and network isolation requirements.
